text:
Kait: Quick PSA - new contractor couldn't finish quickstart. CLI docs show RW_API_KEY but our Ruby sample uses REDWOOD_SECRET and they copied that -> 403.
Miguel: Yikes. Where did REDWOOD_SECRET come from? Was that an old experiment?
Chen: That var was introduced in a side branch last year for short-lived tokens. It shouldn't be in published snippets.
Kait: So we have three names floating: RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_SECRET. That's definitely onboarding friction.
DocsBot: Config guide v1.1: canonical env var = RW_API_KEY. REDWOOD_API_KEY allowed as legacy. REDWOOD_SECRET deprecated; remove from samples.
Miguel: Action items: 1) sweep README samples and replace with RW_API_KEY 2) add SDK helper get_api_key() that tries RW_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_SECRET -> creds file -> metadata 3) graceful error message listing which vars were checked.
Chen: Also add support for X-Redwood-Key-Id header to enable key rotation without env changes. Ops asked for that.
Kait: For long-running services, expose a credential provider/callback so processes can refresh keys at runtime. Add an example in the long-running-workers section.
Miguel: I want a tiny telemetry ping when fallback/legacy var used (non-identifying). Make it opt-out via RW_TELEMETRY=0. That will tell us how many users still rely on REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_SECRET.
Chen: Agreed, but run it through Security review. No key material should ever be sent. Only a tag like "env_source:legacy".
Kait: I'll open PRs: docs sweep + Ruby/JS/Python sample fixes. Miguel will add helper in SDKs. Chen will coordinate header format with Security and add rotation docs.
SupportBot: New ticket DE-5012 created: "env var parity + rotation header" assigned to @Kait, @Miguel, @Chen.
Kait: Temporary workaround for support teams: tell users to `export RW_API_KEY=<key>` and retry. I'll add that to theKB. :thumbsup:
Miguel: Also add CI matrix test that runs quickstart with each of the legacy vars set alone so we catch regressions.
Chen: And a small lint rule that flags `REDWOOD_SECRET` in docs so we don't accidentally reintroduce it.
Kait: Cool. I'll push the docs PR and ping this channel when it's live.
Miguel: Thanks all. Short-term, let's mark REDWOOD_SECRET as deprecated in the SDKs with a clear warning when used.
